hero.eyebrow: Free · open source · first stable release
hero.title: Run all your AI coding agents. Answer only the ones that need you.
hero.tagline: A free desktop app that puts your GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and Codex sessions in one office, with an inbox for every agent waiting on your OK.
hero.alt: Agent Durbar with simulated data: folders as rooms, agents at desks, a 'Needs you 5' button and one agent waiting for permission to rename a tool
hero.caption: Simulator demo data: names, costs and tasks are invented.
hero.nameNote: Why “Durbar”? A durbar is a royal court where everyone gets a hearing. Here your agents are the court, and you decide who gets your attention.

status: Stable v0.1.4 · unsigned · used by hand on Linux and on real Macs; on Windows it was tried once by hand on a real PC (2026-10-21) and is checked in CI (builds start on all three, and real-account end-to-end runs passed on all three, 9 of 9, 2026-10-20).

cards.title: Never miss a waiting agent
cards.text: One inbox for every agent waiting on you, oldest first, with how long each has waited. Answer with a click or a key.

cards.title: Read-only until you say so
cards.text: Every agent starts Read-only. Switch to Ask first or Allow all only when you choose, per agent, any time.

cards.title: Cap the spend per session
cards.text: Cost estimates per folder and spending limits per session. Usage bills against your own plans: Durbar never charges you.

cards.title: Any folder: code, docs, notes
cards.text: A room is a folder an agent works in: code, documents, research or notes.

howItWorks.title: Install and connect
howItWorks.text: Connect the AI account you already have. Settings > Agent apps can install the agent app and sign you in with the vendor's own page.
howItWorks.alt: Settings > Agent apps with Copilot, Claude Code and Codex and one next step each
howItWorks.caption: Settings > Agent apps: each app with its state and one next step.

howItWorks.title: Add a folder
howItWorks.text: Each folder becomes a room in the office, with one or more agents at its desks.

howItWorks.title: Chat, approve, watch
howItWorks.text: Open an agent to chat. Approve what it asks, and keep an eye on every other agent in the strip and the office.

aiTheme.text: …or describe your own and let AI make it.

harnesses.name: GitHub Copilot
harnesses.verified: Checked on a real account since the first milestone, with the Copilot runtime from the official SDK and your own login.
harnesses.notYet: Checked on Copilot Pro (2026-10-20): switching between two real models, the long-context tier and compact-and-switch work. Copilot's own runtime does not stop at a spending limit, so Durbar enforces the limit itself.

harnesses.name: Claude Code
harnesses.verified: Checked on a real account: every mode, stop, resume, models, questions, MCP, sub-agents, the cost limit and summaries.
harnesses.notYet: Installed, signed in and answering on Linux, macOS and Windows CI machines (end-to-end run, 2026-10-20); used by hand on a real Windows PC only once (2026-10-21), not day to day.

harnesses.name: OpenAI Codex
harnesses.verified: Checked on a real account: every mode, resume, models, history, questions, MCP tools, sub-agents and summaries; signed in with an API key and answering on Linux, macOS and Windows CI machines (end-to-end run, 2026-10-20).
harnesses.notYet: Read-only and Ask first need Codex's own sandbox: on Ubuntu 24.04+ that takes an AppArmor profile, and on Windows Codex's elevated sandbox. Not yet used by hand on a Windows PC.

safety.title: Read-only by default
safety.text: A new agent starts Read-only: edits, commands and other changes are denied. Ask first makes it wait for your OK; Allow all asks once to confirm. Durbar asks agents to stay in their folders; only Codex is held there by its own sandbox.

safety.title: No tokens stored, no telemetry
safety.text: Each agent app reads its own sign-in. Durbar has no accounts, no servers of its own and no telemetry.

safety.title: You set the spending limit
safety.text: Give a session a spending limit in credits or dollars. Limits are soft by one call: the call already running finishes and can go a little over (and the first message after a resume may not be held); then the chat asks you what to do.

proof: Built in the open and spec-driven: every feature has a public spec that says what was checked and what is a known gap.

faq.q: What is an AI agent here?
faq.a: An assistant that works on its own in a folder: it reads files, runs commands and makes changes, and stops to ask when it needs you. GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and OpenAI Codex are such agents; Durbar lets you watch and answer several at once.

faq.q: Do I need all three agent apps?
faq.a: No. One is enough: GitHub Copilot (a free plan works), Claude Code or OpenAI Codex. Durbar shows the ones you have and can install the others for you.

faq.q: Which accounts or keys do I need?
faq.a: The ones those apps already use: your GitHub account for Copilot, a Claude plan or an Anthropic API key for Claude Code, a ChatGPT plan or an OpenAI API key for Codex. Each app keeps its own sign-in; Durbar never sees your tokens.

faq.q: Does my code go anywhere new?
faq.a: No. Durbar runs on your computer and has no servers, accounts or telemetry of its own. The agent apps talk to their own vendors exactly as they do without Durbar.
Each person installs it on their own computer and uses their own plans. There is no shared server and nothing to administer.
Durbar is free and open source (MIT). The agents bill your own plans; Durbar shows estimates and lets you set spending limits.
No. A room is any folder an agent works in: code, documents, research or notes.
